candidates.requirement: Call json_tokener_parse_ex more than once on the same tokener to exercise saved number and exponent state.
candidates.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates tok, calls json_tokener_parse_ex once with all input bytes, then frees tok.
candidates.failure_condition: A split input such as successive chunks "[0", "e+", "-]" requires retained parser state; the target cannot make the second or third call.
candidates.alternative_paths: Putting those bytes in one fuzz input does not exercise restoration from a prior call. Each entry creates a fresh tokener, and the complete harness has no other parse call.

candidates.requirement: Set JSON_TOKENER_STRICT on the tokener before parsing to reach strict rejection of a missing exponent.
candidates.target_route: The target parses once with a newly allocated, zero-initialized tokener and never sets flags.
candidates.failure_condition: With strict mode, the finite input "[0e]" is rejected as a number error; the target can only exercise its default-mode acceptance.
candidates.alternative_paths: Input bytes cannot set tok->flags. The complete harness has no set_flags call or other tokener setup, and the parser guards the strict outcome on that flag.

before.requirement: Reach the specific restored exponent-state validation for successive chunks such as "[0", "e+", "-]".
before.reason: The before number state starts its exponent tracking anew on each call and has no saved-exponent reconstruction. Its broader incremental parsing is a different capability.

after.requirement: Reach saved-exponent reconstruction and rejection when number text spans parse_ex calls.
after.reason: The after parser reconstructs exponent state from saved text; the harness frees the tokener after its sole parse call.

source_evidence.quote:
* Fix incremental parsing of numbers, especially those with exponents, e.g.
   so parsing "[0", "e+", "-]" now properly returns an error.

claims.reason: The new restoration capability is absent before and required after; the harness's one-call structure is unchanged.

before.requirement: Reject an incomplete exponent such as "[0e]" specifically in strict mode.
before.reason: The before number path passes the saved text to the earlier double parser without the after-source full-length conversion check or strict-mode trimming distinction.

after.requirement: Set JSON_TOKENER_STRICT and reach full-length rejection of "[0e]".
after.reason: Strict mode leaves the incomplete exponent untrimmed, and full-length conversion rejects it; the harness never sets strict mode.

source_evidence.quote:
/* The behavior when missing the exponent varies slightly */
    {"0e", 2, 2, json_tokener_continue, 1},
    {"0e", 3, 2, json_tokener_success, 1},
    {"0e", 3, 2, json_tokener_error_parse_eof, 1, JSON_TOKENER_STRICT},
    {"[0e]", -1, -1, json_tokener_success, 1},
    {"[0e]", -1, 3, json_tokener_error_parse_number, 1, JSON_TOKENER_STRICT},

claims.reason: The same strict missing-exponent outcome is assessed on both sides; it is supported only after the changed parser path, and the old harness still lacks flag setup.
